findings.claim: Initial list-load failures now expose an empty array as data instead of leaving data undefined, breaking the stated TanStack-compatible hook shape on error.
findings.evidence: `useRuntimeList` calls `toQueryResult(..., list.items, list.items.length > 0)`, and `toQueryResult` returns `value` whenever `!state.isLoading`; on an initial failed list load `list.items` is `[]`, `isLoading` is false, and `error` is set, so hooks like `useAgents()` return `{ data: [], isError: true }`. Acceptance requires unchanged app hook return shapes and failures exposed as error states; TanStack Query initial failures have `data: undefined`, not an empty successful-looking list.
findings.suggested_fix: Track whether the list has successfully loaded at least once, or pass a success/hasFetched flag from the graph list state, and keep `data` undefined when the initial fetch failed.

findings.claim: The change records a known test coverage gap for the new post-stream SessionTranscript invalidation path.
findings.evidence: Warning constraint `tests-for-new-features` says tests should exist for new hooks, stores and utilities; verification.md states: `The post-stream SessionTranscript invalidation ... is implemented in use-chat-runtime.ts but only exercised indirectly ... there is no dedicated unit test`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a focused test around `useChatRuntime` stream completion that asserts `invalidateEntity(ENTITY.SessionTranscript, threadId)` is called or that the transcript entity becomes stale.
